classes.name: RFog
classes.comment: Singleton: RFog::Init 8b690 allocates 0x1c and stores the object in global 0x1ec004. No USingleton base (ctor 7d930 stores only its own vtable 0x191514, 3 slots). Fields sit at identical offsets on PS2 (vptr at +0 on both).

fields.name: fogInfo
fields.evidence: ctor 7d930 allocates a separate 0x1c-byte block and stores it here, then fills it: +0 1.0, +4 fog end (copied from +0x14), +8 density 0.000476, +0xc int 3 (mode), +0x10 colour 0x80856838, +0x14 5000.0, +0x18 scale 1.0; tuning-DB attribs bound to its members. FogColour 7d790 reads it; PS2 +0x4 in FogInfo/FogColour/CalcFogEnd. Pointee type unknown (fog-parameters struct). Name invented

fields.name: scaling
fields.evidence: UpdateScale 7d8c0 tests byte +0x8 and clears it when the fade ends; ctor zeroes it. PS2 +0x8 is a 4-byte int (SetFogScale/UpdateScale). Name invented

fields.name: scaleEndFrame
fields.evidence: UpdateScale compares it with the frame counter global 0x1f2a4c and uses (end - now) as the remaining time; PS2 +0xc written by SetFogScale. Name invented

fields.name: scaleRate
fields.evidence: UpdateScale: remaining * [+0x10] subtracted from +0x18 gives the current scale; PS2 SetFogScale(float,float) writes +0x10 float. Name invented

fields.name: targetScale
fields.evidence: ctor sets 1.0; UpdateScale copies it into fogInfo+0x18 when the fade ends; PS2 +0x18 float in SetFogScale/UpdateScale. Name invented

notes: Singleton globals (Init stores the new object): RFog 0x1ec004, RColorize 0x1f6898, RDecalManager 0x1fe820, RGain 0x200f20, RParticulate 0x201754, RPostProcessing 0x20175c, RSniperZoom 0x201818. None has a USingleton base: every ctor stores only its own 3-slot vtable and calls no base ctor.

All nine classes keep the same field offsets on PS2 and Xbox (vptr at +0 on both where present); only bool widths differ (RFog +8, RSniperZoom +4, RParticulate +0xffc are 1 byte on Xbox, 4 on PS2) and padding follows each, so nothing moves.

RGain on Xbox is a different implementation: PS2 only has gain/offset (+4..+0x20); Xbox adds a material (+0x24), an EAGL::DynamicModel (+0x70) and a parameter-binding block (+0xd8..+0x12b) pointing back at the material, +0xc8, gain and offset. Binding-block field names are guesses.
REmpBolts +0x18: MSVC std::map/set on Xbox (12 bytes), a FastFree'd pointer on PS2; the two PS2 GetRandomAnchor overloads use +0x10/+0x14 and +0x18 respectively.
RTyreTrack segment layout (32 bytes per segment, 64 or 32 segments) comes from the ctor's maxSegments*32 indexing; the +0x800 region is PS2 evidence only.

USimpleMaterial / USimpleTexturedMaterial / ROffscreenBuffer / EAGL::DynamicModel members are byte arrays (0x60, 0x60, 0x24, 0x58 by position) because the types are not in Ghidra; the 0x60 material sizes assume the member runs to the end of the object.
RFog::UpdateScale 7d8c0 tail-jumps to SetFogParams 7d840, so its return type follows SetFogParams (left unset).
RVehicle::TriggerEmpBolts 95a10 allocates REmpBolts with size 0x22c (only caller of the ctor).
